title: Whole-Document Extraction Output
description: The only shapes the language model steps of a whole-document extraction job may return (ADR 0010): an outline answer (pass 1, one per chunk, outline carried forward) or a section answer (pass 2, one per chunk, against the frozen outline). The API sends a strict-compatible form of the one it asks for and validates against it. Handles are per job: cN are existing concepts of the import's company sent as candidates (c0 its root, at most 200 per call); oN are outline nodes, numbered by the API in the order they were accepted and stable for the whole job; kN are keys of new nodes inside one answer. There is no depth limit. A node or intent may attach under any node of the outline, at any depth, by handle, by an earlier key, or by a path of labels from the company root; the only ceilings are the job's total drafts (ONTAIX_DOCUMENT_EXTRACTION_MAX_NODES, default 2,000) and its token budget (ONTAIX_DOCUMENT_EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS). The maxItems below are the absolute contract bound per answer. Every free-text field refuses markup (< and >), C0 and C1 control characters, DEL, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029 and every Unicode format character (category Cf) in the Basic Multilingual Plane, exactly as contracts/teach-extraction.schema.json does; the API's normalisation step also refuses every Cf character outside that plane. Grounding (ADR 0008 rule, unchanged): every new label - an outline node's label and every newLabel of an intent - must equal, after normalisation, a run of whole words of the sentence named by sentenceIndex, allowing singular or plural; the drafted label is sliced from the document text, never taken from the model. A label that fails is dropped (unresolved, reason ungrounded_label) and so are the nodes and intents that depend on it. The model chooses structure - parents, actions, domains - but never invents a label. Answer-invalidating checks: a rel intent without an action, or a spec intent with one (schema); unique keys; a key cited as a parent or end is defined earlier in the answer; every handle was sent; every normalised action (NFKC, whitespace runs collapsed to one space, trimmed, lower-cased) is neither is a nor equivalent to; sentenceIndex lies in the chunk; no node or intent joins a concept to itself. Any failure makes that chunk's answer invalid; the chunk is listed as unresolved (model_invalid_output) and the job continues. The answer is requested as compact JSON.

ref.description: Where a node attaches or what an intent cites: a handle the API sent (cN an existing concept of the company, c0 its root; oN a node of the outline built so far), the key of a node earlier in the same answer, or a path of labels from the company root down to the parent, of any length. A path is resolved by the API against the whole outline and the company's concepts, one normalised label per level; a path that does not resolve drops the node or intent (unresolved, reason unknown_parent).

path.description: Labels root-first, starting below the company root. No maximum length: paths of any depth are allowed.

nodes.description: New outline nodes this chunk adds, parents before children. Nodes the chunk only mentions again are not repeated; a node whose normalised label equals an outline node or a sent candidate is that node or concept.

label.description: No leading or trailing space. Must be grounded: the words appear in the document sentence named by sentenceIndex.

action.description: The birth relation's action, read parent to child, for example runs, includes or consists of. After normalisation, is a and equivalent to are refused.

role.description: Advisory: what the node is in the business. Shown to the reviewer in the draft note; it does not limit where the node may sit.

domainKey.description: The domain template of the node; absent to inherit from its parent (production under the root).

sentenceIndex.description: The document sentence the words come from; it lies in the chunk the API sent (the overlap included).

span.description: A verbatim quote of the words in that sentence. The API locates it as in ADR 0008 (Source ranges).

kind.description: As in teach extraction: rel is subject action object; spec is subject is a kind of object, both ends in the import's company.

action.description: Required for rel, absent for spec. After normalisation, is a and equivalent to are refused.

sentenceIndex.description: The document sentence the words come from; it lies in the chunk the API sent (the overlap included).

span.description: A verbatim quote of the words in that sentence. The API locates it as in ADR 0008 (Source ranges).

intentRef.description: An outline node or candidate by handle, a node by path of labels, or a new grounded label. A new label as object of a rel intent whose subject exists is born under the subject.

newLabel.description: No leading or trailing space. Must be grounded: the words appear in the document sentence named by sentenceIndex.
